test_policy.notes: International students are not required to submit SAT or ACT; if sent they will be considered. Domestic (nonresident) admission uses cumulative unweighted high school GPA only and states test scores are not used. College Navigator (IPEDS) lists SAT/ACT as not considered (test blind). SAT EBRW 450 or ACT English 18 can also prove English proficiency.

requirements.notes: Boise State does not accept the Common App; use the Boise State application. International first-year file: application, $85 non-refundable fee (no waivers for international students), high school transcripts or marksheets (unofficial accepted for review; official required later), proof of English proficiency, passport name page. Considered mainly on past academic achievement; no minimum GPA is published for international applicants (domestic nonresidents are automatically admitted at 3.00 unweighted). Recommendations and personal statement are optional. Decisions typically within two weeks of a complete file. Admitted F-1 applicants must send a Financial Documentation Form and proof of funds.

deadlines.label: Merit scholarship deadline (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: All admission materials (application, fee, English scores, transcripts, passport copy) must be received by this date for automatic merit scholarship consideration. The International Admissions home page also shows a Global Scholarships deadline of March 1 but under outdated 'Fall 2025' labels; the scholarships page lists Dec. 15, 2026 for fall 2027.

deadlines.label: Priority application deadline (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: Fall priority date from the international first-year page (printed without a year; treated as fall 2027). No later final international deadline is published; decisions are rolling. Spring 2027: Oct. 1, 2026 for both priority and scholarships.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exempt with 3 or more years of secondary education in English-medium schools in an approved country list (e.g. US, UK, Ireland, Canada excl. Quebec, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Jamaica). Other accepted proof: ACT English 18, SAT EBRW 450, AP English Language or Literature 3, IB English A 4 (completed IB Diploma within 2 years), IGCSE/O Level English C, WASSCE B3 and others. The office may ask for more proof case by case. Applicants below the minimums are considered for the Pathway Program: Accelerated 1 semester (IELTS 5.5, TOEFL 62-67, Duolingo 86-99), Standard 2 semesters (IELTS 5.0, TOEFL 45-61, Duolingo 75-85), Extended 3 semesters (IELTS 4.5, TOEFL 38-44, Duolingo 65-74); on completion students are fully admitted to their degree program, tuition is the nonresident rate less about a 30% scholarship, and Pathway students are not eligible for merit scholarships.

cost.notes: International undergraduate estimate for 2026-27 from Boise State International Admissions: tuition and fees $29,477 (published as one figure), room and board $16,894, books $800, health insurance $2,175 and personal $2,203 (other_usd = 2,175 + 2,203), total $51,549. Pathway Program total is $38,427. Idaho resident tuition does not apply to international students.

aid.notes: International undergraduates are automatically considered for merit scholarships of $5,000 to $17,000 per year if materials are complete by the deadline: Non-Resident scholarship ($5,000 at 3.10-3.29 cumulative unweighted GPA, $10,000 at 3.30+; the Financial Aid Office page names these Ridgeline and Summit with slightly different GPA bands) plus a Global Scholarship for international students only ($5,000 at 3.50-3.749, $6,000 at 3.75-3.999, $7,000 at 4.00+), capped at $17,000 total. Global awards depend on availability. First-year awards are renewable for up to four years (eight semesters). Not available for Nursing, Pre-Nursing, Construction Management, Radiological Science, online or self-supported programs, and not for Pathway students. No fully funded scholarships. Need-based aid for international students is not described.
